title.narrative: Improved governance of labour migration and protection of migrant workers in line with ILS

description.narrative: In the context of the realization of its national development plan (Vision 2030), Saudi Arabia has initiated a range of important reforms relating to labour market governance, including the governance of foreign employment and improved protections for migrant workers, with a view also to addressing forced labour practices. Building on these efforts, the outcome aims to support the effective implementation and further strengthening of labour market policies and institutions in line with relevant international labour standards. Migrant workers, including domestic workers, as well as employers and workers’ organizations, benefit from strengthened regulatory frameworks and improved labour market functioning. This includes enhanced regulation of recruitment agencies and labour supply companies, strengthened internal labour market mobility for migrant workers, and improved protections for domestic workers. The International Labour Organization will work in close collaboration with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, and representative employers’ and workers’ organizations, to strengthen the evidence base, deepen understanding of labour market dynamics, and build the capacities of national stakeholders. Further progress in the areas of recruitment, internal labour mobility and domestic work will be advanced in consultation with national stakeholders.
